newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Briton appointed U.N. envoy for Kabila's Congo.
newsitem.headline: Briton appointed U.N. envoy for Kabila's Congo.

text.p: A British development official was appointed on Monday as Secretary-General Kofi Annan's special representative for President Laurent Kabila's Democratic Republic of the Congo, the United Nations announced.

The appointment of Robin Kinlock, human resource director for the U.N. Development Programme (UNDP) in New York, overlaps with that of Mohamed Sahnoun, an Algerian diplomat who is currently Annan's special envoy for the region.

U.N. officials said that with Kabila in power, it was necessary to base a senior envoy in Kinsasha. Sahnoun, they said, would handle the remainder of the region or events concerning Kinshasa and its neighbours.
Kinloch was director of UNDP's Africa bureau and chief of its West Africa division from 1987 to 1991. Before that he spent five years as UNDP 's resident representative in the former Zaire.
